question: If tanA = (1)/(sqrt{10)}, A is an acute angle, then the value of sinA + cosecA is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

From tanA = 1/√10, we directly get Perpendicular (P) = 1 and Base (B) = √10.

Hypotenuse (H) = √(P² + B²) = √(1 + 10) = √11.

Substitute values into sinA + cosecA = (P/H) + (H/P).

sinA + cosecA = (1/√11) + (√11/1) = (1 + 11) / √11 = 12/√11.

**∴ The correct answer is 12/√11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f17cd1eca4ea009bbf2267d3c2860753af42342de08927a7dd53afdacf08f0ee.png] 

**Given:**

tanA = 1 / √10

**Formula Used:**

tanθ = Perpendicular / Base

sinθ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse

cosecθ = Hypotenuse / Perpendicular

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Perpendicular (P) = 1 and Base (B) = √10

⇒ Using Pythagoras Theorem: H² = P² + B²

⇒ H = √(1² + (√10)²)

⇒ H = √(1 + 10) = √11

⇒ Now, substitute the values of P and H to find sinA and cosecA:

⇒ sinA = P / H = 1 / √11

⇒ cosecA = H / P = √11 / 1 = √11

⇒ Add both the values: sinA + cosecA = (1 / √11) + √11

⇒ sinA + cosecA = (1 + √11 × √11) / √11

⇒ sinA + cosecA = (1 + 11) / √11 = 12 / √11

**∴ The correct answer is 12/√11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

In a right-angled triangle, the sine function represents the ratio of the Perpendicular to the Hypotenuse, while the cosine function represents the Base to the Hypotenuse.

Reciprocal Identities

Each primary trigonometric ratio has a reciprocal: cosecθ = 1/sinθ, secθ = 1/cosθ, and cotθ = 1/tanθ.

Pythagorean Identities

The foundational identity is sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, from which 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ can be derived.
